object_label: setting up the Doodle poll
evidence_sentence: Thank you, Sunita, for your initiative in drafting the screencast outline and setting up the Doodle poll.
full_email_context: Thread ID: E0OL9G Mail ID: MAILE7104DPS Date: 11th April 2020 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> Subject: Re: Coordination Call for JCDL 2020 Camera-Ready Revisions – Doodle Poll & Screencast Outline Feedback  Dear Sunita, Michael, and Ramesh,  Thank you, Sunita, for your initiative in drafting the screencast outline and setting up the Doodle poll. I have just filled out my availability, with a slight preference for Thursday at 16:00 BST, though I can be flexible if Friday suits everyone better.  I reviewed your preliminary outline and found the structure logical and well-matched to the reviewers’ requests. Including a modular stepwise walkthrough (with short highlight annotations) of the provenance workflow should mitigate concerns about reproducibility and onboarding for new users. I suggest briefly touching on two common annotation edge cases (perhaps with an example from the Bengali-English corpus section), to demonstrate the workflow’s adaptability. Please let me know if you would like materials or sample datasets for those segments—I am happy to share excerpts from my previous FAIR pipeline slides.  Regarding the ACM reproducibility visual, I will prepare a high-resolution graphic and updated slide by tomorrow and upload both assets to the “Revision_Materials” folder. Feel free to reference the new slide in your video, or keep it a separate mention if you prefer.  Ramesh, once your succinct corpus period/context note for the ambiguous mapping schematic is ready, kindly upload or forward it so we can integrate across all channels.  Thank you all again for the coordination and momentum. I look forward to locking in our meeting time to finalize the division of tasks. With our current synergy, I am optimistic we can assemble the camera-ready submission ahead of the 15 July deadline.  Best regards,  Ananya

full_email_context: Thread ID: CX1HWB Mail ID: MAIL0Z27NQY4 Date: 3rd June 2020 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> Subject: Re: Minutes and Action Items: JOCCH Article Planning Meeting (16 August)  Dear Sunita, Michael, and Ramesh,  Thank you, Sunita, for the thorough documentation of our meeting discussions and for clearly outlining the upcoming deliverables and responsibilities. I confirm that the minutes accurately reflect both the substance and spirit of our planning, and I appreciate the clarity around section assignments and compliance steps.  To follow up on my action item regarding the draft lay abstract: I will circulate an initial version to the group by 18 August. I plan to synthesize feedback from our prior outreach workshops and emphasize the societal relevance and interpretability of our NLP tools for historical corpora, as discussed. Once drafted, I invite everyone’s input to ensure our summary is accessible and compelling for both a general and an academic audience, per ACM JOCCH’s requirements.  Regarding Oxford’s compliance aspects for repository hosting, I have reviewed the latest guidance. There are no additional restrictions for joint open data releases as long as attribution is thorough and embargoed data are clearly marked—in alignment with the IACS and Stanford protocols presented by Ramesh and Michael. I will append a concise Oxford compliance statement to the shared supplement before final submission.  If any co-author foresees delays in their assigned sections or supplementary material contributions, please flag these at the earliest so we can coordinate support or adjust deadlines as needed. I look forward to working with all of you to bring this comprehensive paper to completion.  Best regards,  Ananya

evidence_sentence: status remains under editorial review.
full_email_context: Thread ID: 0IDUSW Mail ID: MAILE0B2F6KD Date: 12th April 2022 From: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> Subject: Minutes and Action Points from 16 October Progress Review  Dear Sunita, Ananya, and Michael,  Thank you all for your participation and focused engagement in yesterday’s progress review. I am writing to circulate the official minutes and summarized action points from our 16 October call, as agreed:  **Participants**: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia (chair), Dr. Ananya Chatterjee, Dr. Michael Bradley, Ms. Sunita Sen   **Date/Time**: 11th April 2020, 15:30–16:25 IST   **Platform**: Google Meet  **Agenda Review and Outcomes:** 1. **JOCCH Submission Status (SUB-JOCCH-2022-0362):**    - No new communications from JOCCH as of the meeting date; status remains under editorial review. Team agreed to maintain daily monitoring of shared inboxes and immediate information relay protocol. 2. **Press/Outreach Coordination:**    - All partner institutions have affirmed press office readiness for embargo-compliant, joint outreach. No procedural discrepancies noted; latest harmonized outreach materials are archived on the shared drive. 3. **Embargo Monitoring Log:**    - Sunita presented the updated log (ver. 14Oct2022). Michael’s harmonization notes were discussed with consensus to finalize tracked changes by 20 October. No pending queries. 4. **Prospects for Joint JCDL 2022 Submission:**    - Agreed to initiate a collaborative documentation folder outlining possible abstract themes and dataset extensions, with a target for draft brainstorming by mid-December. 5. **Other Business:**    - All members reconfirmed Q&A compliance status. Ananya will touch base with Oxford’s legal counsel regarding embargo expiry ramifications, should a pre-acceptance press query arise.  **Action Points:** - Sunita and Michael to finalize embargo log harmonization and update master sheet by 20 October. - Prof. Bhatia (myself) to draft a shared follow-up template for unforeseen press queries and circulate by 22 October. - Ananya to open JCDL 2022 joint documentation workspace and notify team by 25 October.  Please reply with any additions or corrections to these minutes by 19 October. Otherwise, I will consider them ratified for consortium records. Thank you for prompt attention and continued collaboration.  Best regards,  Prof. Ramesh Bhatia   Professor, Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

After a careful review of both the consolidated compliance supplement and the updated manuscript drafts, I want to share a few final remarks ahead of our full-draft circulation for group review, as planned for our 1 September target.  First, the merged compliance document presents a consistent and professionally unified representation of our multi-institutional commitments. Sunita, I noted that you addressed both my and Ananya’s minor comments on terminology, particularly harmonizing phrases regarding archival embargoes and open-access provisions. The resulting text should satisfy JOCCH’s editorial requirements and facilitate a seamless file upload.  Turning to the manuscript, I have commented in the “Evaluation & Benchmarks” and “Core Manuscript” folders regarding the introduction of our hybrid metrics—especially the balance between precision in named entity recognition and recall across temporal strata. Ananya, your revisions to the “Transfer Learning in Low-Resource Historical Texts” subsection are clear and well-positioned; I suggest we further cross-reference your methods flowchart with the experimental results tables to give reviewers direct evidence of effectiveness.  Ramesh, the profiling framework in your section provides a robust context for our dataset curation choices. One point for final alignment: shall we add a concise paragraph linking “Profiling” conclusions with our inter-annotator agreement statistics? I believe this would help foreground the reproducibility of our annotation strategy.  In summary, we appear well-positioned to begin our comprehensive internal review, with all draft components and supplements available for feedback. Looking forward to your responses and any additional suggestions before we finalize the manuscript package for submission.  Many thanks and best regards,  Michael

full_email_context: Thread ID: 8J4MZ8 Mail ID: MAILU3CVH92B Date: 10th March 2021 From: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> To: JOCCH Editorial Office <jocch@acm.org> CC: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Submission of Minor Galley Proof Corrections – SUB-JOCCH-2021-0612  Dear JOCCH Editorial Office,  On behalf of my co-authors, I am submitting our consolidated list of minor corrections for the galley proofs of our article “HistocrNLP: A Reproducible NLP Pipeline for Historical Texts across Domains” (Submission ID: SUB-JOCCH-2021-0612), along with the marked PDF as per the requested procedure. We greatly appreciate the editorial and production teams’ careful work and are pleased to report that the manuscript and supplementary materials are in excellent shape.  Please see below the specific corrections we request:  1. **Table 1:** Adjust the alignment of the final column (rightmost) for uniformity with the table’s aesthetic and improve readability. 2. **Author Contact Detail:** On page 14, please correct Dr. Michael Bradley’s institutional email to “michael@cs.stanford.edu” (currently appears as “michael@cs.stanford”). 3. **Supplementary Material Reference:** On page 22, we recommend that the call-out box for the supplementary HTML download link be given a shaded background, in line with ACM accessibility guidelines, in order to enhance visual distinction for readers with accessibility needs. 4. **Typographical Issue:** In the section titled “Domain Adaptation Results,” there is a stray hyphen at the end of the section that should be removed.  I have attached the marked-up PDF highlighting these locations and suggestions.  With these minor corrections incorporated, we are confident the article will be ready for online publication. If any further clarification or documentation is needed from our side, please let me know at your convenience.  Thank you for your continued assistance and for shepherding our article through the final production stages.  Best regards,  Sunita Sen   (on behalf of Prof. Ramesh Bhatia, Dr. Michael Bradley, and Dr. Ananya Chatterjee)   PhD Scholar, Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science   scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in

full_email_context: Thread ID: S3VO9L Mail ID: MAIL7Z6LCTYX Date: 16th September 2024 From: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> To: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> Subject: Revision Task Progress—Embargo Policy Update for JOCCH Resource Note  Dear Ananya, Ramesh, and Michael,  Thank you for outlining a clear revision plan following the positive JOCCH decision. I am pleased to confirm that I have begun drafting an expanded clarification on the 'rolling embargo' mechanism, as requested by the editorial office. My current draft for Section 3.2 delineates the timeline and criteria under which supplementary datasets—specifically, Part II of the “Bengal Gazette” and Part III of the “Madras Chronicle”—will be released post-embargo. I have referenced both our original partner MOUs and the Zenodo best practices for phased data disclosure.  To address the editorial comment regarding future updates, I have added a sentence explicitly indicating our intention to provide accession links and updated metadata in the online supplementary material each time a dataset segment transitions out of embargo. I have also drawn sample language from recent compliance appendices in JOCCH, ensuring our wording aligns with accepted conventions.  I will upload my full draft as a marked revision (docx and PDF) to the “2024_JournalExtension/Revision_Materials” folder by 24 August. Feedback or suggested refinements from any of you would be welcome prior to integration with the main manuscript.  Michael—please let me know if you need copies of our original embargo tables for diagram annotation. Ramesh and Ananya—I look forward to any suggestions you may have to further strengthen the clarity and compliance of this section.  Looking forward to continuing our smooth and efficient revision process. Please advise if there are other related compliance considerations you would like addressed at this stage.  Best regards,  Sunita  Sunita Sen   PhD Scholar   Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

full_email_context: Thread ID: R0CFUU Mail ID: MAIL4V8XZUP2 Date: 13th January 2022 From: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: ACL 2022 Acceptance – Next Steps and Preparation Timeline  Dear Prof. Bhatia, Michael, and Ananya,  I hope you have received the wonderful news: our paper “NLP Methods for Historical Data: Provenance and Bias Mitigation” has been officially ACCEPTED for presentation at ACL 2022 (SUB-ACL-2022-0047). Congratulations to each of you for your dedicated collaboration and expert contributions throughout this lengthy process.  To ensure we meet all post-acceptance requirements and prepare efficiently for the conference, please see below for a consolidated timeline and assigned next steps:  1. **Proofreading and Final Metadata Check**:   Let’s each review the PDF in the submission portal to confirm all author details, figure clarity, and affiliations are correct. Please log your confirmation or required corrections in our shared Google Doc (“ACL2022_AcceptedPaper_FinalReview”) by **10 July**.  2. **Presentation Preparation**:   According to ACL instructions, we will be notified of our assigned oral presentation slot by 15 July and will need to upload a finalized deck between 20–25 July. I propose we hold a group rehearsal once the slot is assigned. I’ve tentatively blocked team availability from 17–19 July for a dry run — please indicate which dates work best for you.  3. **Conference Registration**:   The presenting author must register for ACL by 22 July. I am volunteering, unless anyone else would like to take on the presentation. Please confirm by 9 July if you prefer to present or propose co-presentation.  4. **Camera-Ready Final Corrections**:   ACL may still flag minor issues by 14 July. I’ll monitor the portal for any last-minute notices; please remain available for urgent turnaround if needed.  Please reply with your preferences for rehearsal timing and presentation role. Once again, I want to extend my gratitude to everyone for contributing to this exciting achievement. Looking forward to representing our work at ACL together!  Warm regards,  Sunita Sen   PhD Scholar   Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

full_email_context: Thread ID: R0CFUU Mail ID: MAIL4V8XZUP2 Date: 13th January 2022 From: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: ACL 2022 Acceptance – Next Steps and Preparation Timeline  Dear Prof. Bhatia, Michael, and Ananya,  I hope you have received the wonderful news: our paper “NLP Methods for Historical Data: Provenance and Bias Mitigation” has been officially ACCEPTED for presentation at ACL 2022 (SUB-ACL-2022-0047). Congratulations to each of you for your dedicated collaboration and expert contributions throughout this lengthy process.  To ensure we meet all post-acceptance requirements and prepare efficiently for the conference, please see below for a consolidated timeline and assigned next steps:  1. **Proofreading and Final Metadata Check**:   Let’s each review the PDF in the submission portal to confirm all author details, figure clarity, and affiliations are correct. Please log your confirmation or required corrections in our shared Google Doc (“ACL2022_AcceptedPaper_FinalReview”) by **10 July**.  2. **Presentation Preparation**:   According to ACL instructions, we will be notified of our assigned oral presentation slot by 15 July and will need to upload a finalized deck between 20–25 July. I propose we hold a group rehearsal once the slot is assigned. I’ve tentatively blocked team availability from 17–19 July for a dry run — please indicate which dates work best for you.  3. **Conference Registration**:   The presenting author must register for ACL by 22 July. I am volunteering, unless anyone else would like to take on the presentation. Please confirm by 9 July if you prefer to present or propose co-presentation.  4. **Camera-Ready Final Corrections**:   ACL may still flag minor issues by 14 July. I’ll monitor the portal for any last-minute notices; please remain available for urgent turnaround if needed.  Please reply with your preferences for rehearsal timing and presentation role. Once again, I want to extend my gratitude to everyone for contributing to this exciting achievement. Looking forward to representing our work at ACL together!  Warm regards,  Sunita Sen   PhD Scholar   Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

evidence_sentence: Sunita and I have scheduled a focused working session tomorrow to finalize the draft agenda for the tutorial/workshop.
full_email_context: Thread ID: CVIA7X Mail ID: MAILZ8YJQ47N Date: 2nd October 2022 From: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> To: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Follow-up on Action Items and Workshop Outline Draft  Dear Michael, Sunita, and Ananya,  Thank you, Michael, for meticulously documenting the minutes from our recent check-in meeting. I appreciated the clarity around our respective responsibilities and the actionable timelines, and I am confident that these will facilitate efficient progress as we approach several critical milestones.  As a brief follow-up, I wanted to confirm that Sunita and I have scheduled a focused working session tomorrow to finalize the draft agenda for the tutorial/workshop. Our aim is to incorporate the suggested live demonstration and interactive Q&A segments, with added consideration for accessibility and hands-on engagement, given Ananya’s valuable suggestions. We will also outline a structure for participant feedback and post-event resource dissemination, ensuring sustained impact and inclusivity.  Once the preliminary agenda is compiled—by end of day 10 May—we will upload it to the shared Drive and notify you both for feedback. Ananya, your input regarding suitable engagement formats and alignment with Oxford’s digital scholarship initiatives will be particularly beneficial at that stage. Michael, if you have any recommendations from your experience coordinating in North American contexts, especially regarding time slot preferences or promotional channels, please share them so we can factor these into our planning.  Further, Sunita and I will review the current tabulated OCR error metrics and annotation notes to ensure consistency and completeness before Sunita circulates the structured research note outline on 14 May. I encourage everyone to continue populating the shared Drive with relevant materials to maintain our centralized workflow.  Lastly, please indicate any potential constraints you foresee with the upcoming dates or tasks, so that we can proactively adjust our plan if necessary. Thank you once again for your collaborative spirit and dedication to advancing this project.  Best regards,  Ramesh  Prof. Ramesh Bhatia   Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

full_email_context: Thread ID: 7E2QBQ Mail ID: MAILK7D2QP83 Date: 18th March 2025 From: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Re: Reflection Points & Preliminary Outline for ‘Lessons Learned’ Memo  Dear Sunita, Ramesh, and Ananya,  Thank you, Sunita, for so promptly synthesizing our preliminary reflections and drafting a coherent outline for the ‘Lessons Learned’ memo. I am strongly in favor of your proposal to both document our experience for internal knowledge transfer and consider a short-form publication, particularly given the innovative compliance protocols and metadata harmonization strategies we piloted.  Reflecting on the technical bottlenecks, I want to emphasize the role that shared live logs and “lock-down” periods played during manuscript synchronization. Perhaps we can develop a reproducible template for ‘multi-author version management’ as part of the memo, which could serve as a useful tool or appendix for others. I’d also propose we explicitly mention our approach to handling conflicting annotations and reviewer-driven rapid revision—this process seemed robust and could provide guidance for other geographically dispersed teams.  Regarding dissemination: - I fully support submitting an abstract for the April departmental colloquium. Sunita, please proceed to draft it—happy to review and co-sign as needed. - For the methods note, I can explore alignment with the EMNLP System Demonstrations track, especially highlighting how our annotation and provenance toolkit generalizes beyond strictly historical data tasks. Let’s revisit this once we receive reviewer feedback from JOCCH, as suggested.  Finally, I recommend appending a “do’s and don’ts” checklist, distilled from our experiences, to the final memo—particularly issues around time-zone coordination and rapid integration cycles.  Looking forward to collaborating on the draft and to your thoughts on the above points.  Best regards,  Michael  Dr. Michael Bradley   Department of Computer Science   Stanford University

full_email_context: Thread ID: 9AU14Y Mail ID: MAILFVW39PQ8 Date: 3rd June 2024 From: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Consolidated Materials for Internal Review & Final Agenda for 24 April Meeting  Dear Sunita, Ramesh, and Ananya,  Thank you all for your diligent progress and commitment to the upcoming journal extension and resource efforts. Sunita, your timely upload of the survey introduction and detailed annotation logs is greatly appreciated; the scenarios provided will be invaluable for positioning the user study in both academic and digital humanities contexts.  Following our mutually-agreed timeline, I have consolidated all currently available materials—including Sunita’s finalized logs, Ananya’s normalization guideline draft, my own extended hosting comparison (now including HuggingFace and institutional repository insights), and Ramesh’s preliminary licensing appendix—in the shared drive directory (“2024_JournalExtension/InternalReview_21Apr”). Please review the “ReadMe” in the folder; I have outlined section assignments and highlighted segments for priority feedback.  Agenda for our 24 April meeting is as follows: 1. Review of written section drafts (focus on normalization guidelines, annotation protocol, licensing considerations) 2. Finalization of dataset hosting venue and DOI allocation strategy 3. Discussion and approval of the user study/survey (survey items, introduction, and planned dissemination channels) 4. Assignment of writing/editorial tasks for both journal extension and resource note submission 5. Timeline confirmation for draft revisions and tentative submission windows  Action points prior to the meeting: - All: Please provide inline comments or revision notes in your sections by 23 April. - Ramesh: Kindly upload the finalized legal/licensing summary as soon as available. - Sunita: If able, supplement the dataset documentation with any outstanding meta-annotations or edge-case illustrations. - Ananya: Please flag any external datasets or benchmarks to be cited in the related work.  If you need clarification, don’t hesitate to reach out. Looking forward to a productive internal review and fruitful planning session on Monday.  Best regards,  Michael  Dr. Michael Bradley   Department of Computer Science   Stanford University

full_email_context: Thread ID: R7YH1F Mail ID: MAILW8JGZP21 Date: 29th July 2023 From: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Final Technical Checklist and Last-Minute Session Notes (JCDL 2023)  Dear Ramesh, Sunita, and Ananya,  Thank you, Ramesh, for sharing the refined closing remarks script and for your thoughtful summary of responsibilities and technical procedures. I confirm receipt of the document, and after reviewing the script, I believe it captures our message and voice exceptionally well.  Ahead of our JCDL 2023 presentation, I’d like to offer a consolidated technical checklist to ensure our last preparations go smoothly:  1. **Zoom Room Access:** All presenters to join 20 minutes before our session. I will open the Zoom room and act as initial host; Sunita is co-host for emergency contingencies. 2. **Backup Slide Decks:** Confirmed upload to “JCDL2023_PresentationAssets” shared folder (checked and accessible as of this morning). Please keep your local copies open. 3. **Screen Share Assignments:** Ananya and I will alternate primary/backup screen sharing. If either encounters issues, Sunita will assume immediate control. 4. **Tech-Check Protocol:** Quick sound and video check on joining. Shared WhatsApp group for real-time troubleshooting. 5. **Introduction & Closing:** Sunita—thank you for volunteering to acknowledge the technical staff in your opening. Ramesh’s closing script is timed at ~2 minutes; rehearsed transitions between speakers will keep us on schedule. 6. **Q&A Logistics:** I’ll monitor the chat, and Ananya will support with verbal queries. We have practiced handoff cues and timing, but please use the private Zoom message if urgent adjustments are needed.  **Final Notes:** - If there are program updates or session changes from JCDL organizers over the next 24 hours, let’s circulate immediately. - Please double-check your time zone conversions to avoid any confusion on presentation day.  Thank you all for your meticulous preparation and teamwork through every stage of this project. I am looking forward to sharing the fruits of our collaboration with the wider community at JCDL 2023.  Best wishes,  Michael  Dr. Michael Bradley   Department of Computer Science   Stanford University

full_email_context: Thread ID: R7YH1F Mail ID: MAILW8JGZP21 Date: 29th July 2023 From: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Final Technical Checklist and Last-Minute Session Notes (JCDL 2023)  Dear Ramesh, Sunita, and Ananya,  Thank you, Ramesh, for sharing the refined closing remarks script and for your thoughtful summary of responsibilities and technical procedures. I confirm receipt of the document, and after reviewing the script, I believe it captures our message and voice exceptionally well.  Ahead of our JCDL 2023 presentation, I’d like to offer a consolidated technical checklist to ensure our last preparations go smoothly:  1. **Zoom Room Access:** All presenters to join 20 minutes before our session. I will open the Zoom room and act as initial host; Sunita is co-host for emergency contingencies. 2. **Backup Slide Decks:** Confirmed upload to “JCDL2023_PresentationAssets” shared folder (checked and accessible as of this morning). Please keep your local copies open. 3. **Screen Share Assignments:** Ananya and I will alternate primary/backup screen sharing. If either encounters issues, Sunita will assume immediate control. 4. **Tech-Check Protocol:** Quick sound and video check on joining. Shared WhatsApp group for real-time troubleshooting. 5. **Introduction & Closing:** Sunita—thank you for volunteering to acknowledge the technical staff in your opening. Ramesh’s closing script is timed at ~2 minutes; rehearsed transitions between speakers will keep us on schedule. 6. **Q&A Logistics:** I’ll monitor the chat, and Ananya will support with verbal queries. We have practiced handoff cues and timing, but please use the private Zoom message if urgent adjustments are needed.  **Final Notes:** - If there are program updates or session changes from JCDL organizers over the next 24 hours, let’s circulate immediately. - Please double-check your time zone conversions to avoid any confusion on presentation day.  Thank you all for your meticulous preparation and teamwork through every stage of this project. I am looking forward to sharing the fruits of our collaboration with the wider community at JCDL 2023.  Best wishes,  Michael  Dr. Michael Bradley   Department of Computer Science   Stanford University

I am grateful for the collective focus on both the technical and administrative aspects, which puts us in an excellent position to meet the upcoming ACL deadline.  Please find below a summary of our main action points and next steps, as agreed upon:  **Meeting Minutes (23rd December 2019):** 1. **Slide Deck**: Ananya will upload the revised, higher-resolution versions of the workflow and provenance metadata figures by 13 June. The team agreed that these changes improve accessibility and comply with ACL’s requirements. 2. **Presenter Bios**: All contributors have uploaded their 75-word bios. Sunita to finalize formatting and create the consolidated PDF. 3. **Q&A Document**: Michael and Ananya will jointly expand the model bias section to reflect our approach to corpus diversity controls, with a target completion by 15 June. 4. **Presenter Declaration**: Michael and Ananya to coordinate signatures for Stanford and Oxford institutional compliance forms no later than 16 June. 5. **Final Review and Submission**: Sunita will assemble all updated materials and circulate the camera-ready package for one last group check by 18 June. Targeted submission to ACL is set for 19 June, ensuring we are clear of the 21 June (23:59 AoE) deadline. 6. **Checklist**: Prof. Bhatia will do a final walkthrough of the filled checklist and report any critical gaps, if found, by 17 June.  **Action Items for All:** Please review the updated slide deck and drafts on the Google Drive no later than 16 June, so we have adequate time for confirmation.  If questions arise before the last review window, feel free to contact me directly or reply-all for group consensus. Thank you once again for your commitment, collaboration, and attention to detail as we move toward this milestone.  Best regards,  Sunita Sen   PhD Scholar   Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

full_email_context: Thread ID: 7NOJYO Mail ID: MAILJ92KLD7P Date: 24th January 2021 From: jocch-office@acm.org To: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> Subject: Decision Notification – Minor Revision Outcome (SUB-JOCCH-2020-0047)  Dear Dr. Chatterjee, Prof. Bhatia, Ms. Sen, and Dr. Bradley,  We are writing to inform you of the editorial decision regarding your revised submission to the ACM Journal on Computing and Cultural Heritage (JOCCH), “Cross-Language NLP Pipelines for Noisy Historical Data: Protocols, Benchmarks, and Reproducibility Advances” (Submission ID: SUB-JOCCH-2020-0047).  Following careful assessment by the assigned Associate Editor and consultation with the original reviewers, we are pleased to announce that your manuscript is **conditionally accepted**, pending minor clarifications. The revised manuscript and accompanying materials effectively addressed the initial reviewer and editorial feedback, particularly regarding compliance protocols and reproducibility artifacts.  The Associate Editor and reviewers have requested the following final modifications: - In the Methods section, provide two additional references to recent cross-domain historical corpora to contextualize dataset selection criteria. - In Table 2, further clarify the “Boundary Error” definition in a footnote for improved reader accessibility. - Update the supplementary notebook’s documentation to reference the uploaded compliance protocol and flowchart in the introductory markdown cell.  Please submit a clean, camera-ready version of your manuscript and supplementary files, together with a brief summary of these final clarifications, by **18th February 2019**. Upon receipt and successful technical check, your article will be scheduled for publication in the forthcoming issue.  Detailed reviewer and AE comments are attached as a PDF. Should you have questions about these requests or require a short extension, please contact us directly at jocch-office@acm.org.  Congratulations on this positive outcome, and thank you again for choosing JOCCH.  With best regards,  ACM JOCCH Editorial Office   jocch-office@acm.org

evidence_sentence: Thank you, Sunita, for taking the lead on implementing the documentation edits and for your commitment to keeping the draft on schedule.
full_email_context: Thread ID: XBASHW Mail ID: MAILPQ61VJ8T Date: 7th June 2019 From: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> Subject: Re: Documentation Revisions and Request for Validation Log Update  Dear Sunita, Ananya, and Prof. Bhatia,  Thank you, Sunita, for taking the lead on implementing the documentation edits and for your commitment to keeping the draft on schedule. I am pleased to report that I have now completed the updated run of the technical validation scripts using the most recent batch of summary statistics and representative OCR error cases you uploaded.  The annotated validation logs (v0.2.1) are now available in our shared Drive directory under `/dataset_release_June2019/validation_logs/`. The logs include extended annotator-level confusion matrices, kappa calculations for all error types, and breakdowns by document source. Additionally, I have prepared a 300-word summary paragraph for the “Technical Validation” section that outlines our evaluation metrics (Cohen’s kappa, F1 per class), cross-annotator agreement methodology, and the logging of pipeline version numbers and dependencies for full reproducibility.  Please let me know if you need any clarification on log file contents. full_email_context: Thread ID: GLMTQR Mail ID: MAIL7LXWQY93 Date: 29th September 2022 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> Subject: Re: Next Steps: Blog Post Draft & Research Note Outline  Dear Ramesh, Sunita, and Michael,  Thank you, Ramesh, for outlining the next coordination steps and for the suggestion on setting up a shared resource folder—it will certainly streamline our collaborative drafting process.  I am available for a brief check-in on either 7 or 8 May, preferably 12:00 noon BST (4:30pm IST, 7:00am PST), but I can be flexible if another consensus emerges. Please let me know if those slots work for the rest of you.  Sunita, having your error analysis outline by mid-May will be very helpful, especially as we start shaping the narrative for the ACL Demo track. Once your structure is shared, I will highlight how best to foreground our contributions in terms of interoperability and multilingual applicability—two aspects I believe ACL reviewers will value.  Regarding the workshop planning, thank you, Ramesh and Sunita, for assuming the lead. For the agenda, I suggest incorporating at least one case-driven interactive session, possibly using anonymized data “snippets” to walk participants through common OCR challenges and corresponding solutions. If you draft a participant engagement framework, I am happy to review and align it with feedback from Oxford’s Humanities Digital Scholarship Programme.  Michael, I look forward to your draft blog post and will prepare a brief quote reflecting on the interdisciplinary learning from this collaboration.  Thanks again for keeping the momentum strong. Confirming my availability for a team check-in and eager to move forward with all outlined tasks. full_email_context: Thread ID: 5NCUDJ Mail ID: MAIL4DZ7R2S9 Date: 8th February 2022 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> Subject: Feedback Remarks from ACL Session Chair and Proposed Edits to Annotation Template  Dear Sunita, Michael, and Prof. Bhatia,  Thank you, Sunita, for consolidating and circulating both the feedback synthesis and the reproducibility template—reviewing your materials has deepened my appreciation for the collective insights received from the ACL attendees and further clarified points of expansion for our JOCCH manuscript.  I have now heard back from our ACL session chair (Dr. Elena Markov), who emphasized two additional points worth considering: 1. She specifically encouraged a detailed comparative analysis of annotation protocols in related historical NLP projects, noting that “meta-level reflection on what has—or has not—worked in longitudinal annotation campaigns will add significant value.” 2. There was also a recommendation to append illustrative annotation case studies (both typical and edge cases) as exemplars for future replicators.  I have transcribed Dr. Markov’s feedback and attached it to this email for the group’s reference.  On the annotation reproducibility template, I have left in-line comments and a few structural suggestions in the shared GitHub document (notably, adding a subsection for annotator disagreement resolution workflow and anonymized inter-annotator agreement statistics across language strata). These additions will not only address requests from both our ACL audience and JOCCH guidelines but could also be highlighted in our cover letter as evidence of methodological rigour.  For next steps, I suggest: - We incorporate Dr. Markov’s suggestions in our corpus creation and methods sections, using explicit examples wherever possible. - Once everyone has edited the template by 7 August, Sunita and Prof. Bhatia might coordinate on the final integration into the manuscript draft and supplementary appendix. - Michael, please let us know if the Smith et al. (2021) approach to case study documentation could inform the structure of our examples, or if you see other best practices from the OCR post-correction literature that should be cited.  I look forward to everyone’s feedback and to pushing ahead as our September draft deadline nears. Please let me know if there are any items I can further support before then.  Best wishes,  Ananya  Dr. Ananya Chatterjee   Department of Computer Science   University of Oxford

full_email_context: Thread ID: Y2G8L4 Mail ID: MAILG8B2MJK9 Date: 19th August 2021 From: acl2021@softconf.com To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> CC: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: ACL 2021 Resource Track Decision Notification: Paper SUB-ACL-2021-0842  Dear Sunita Sen and Co-authors,  We are writing with the decision concerning your submission to the ACL 2021 Resource Track:  - Title: Deploying Synthetic Preview and Embargo Protocols for Multilingual Historical NLP Resources - Submission ID: SUB-ACL-2021-0842  After thorough evaluation by the Area Chairs and a panel of expert reviewers, we are pleased to inform you that your submission has been **accepted for presentation** at the ACL 2021 Resource Track, pending the completion of camera-ready revisions incorporating requested minor changes suggested by the reviewers.  **Summary of Reviewer Feedback:** - The reviewers highlighted the strong methodological contributions, especially the reproducibility framework and synthetic sample protocols for sensitive historical data. - Suggestions were made to further clarify the annotation provenance in Section 4 and streamline the compliance appendix for clarity. - Minor formatting and typographical corrections were noted.  **Next Steps:** - Please submit your revised, camera-ready version addressing the reviewers’ minor comments via the Softconf START system by 14th September 2019, 23:59 UTC. - The camera-ready submission instructions, including copyright forms and template updates, are now available through your author portal (https://softconf.com/acl2021/track_resource/). - Ensure all co-author and institutional details are current and correct in the metadata.  Further instructions regarding conference registration and presentation logistics will be provided closer to the event.  Congratulations to you and your team on this accomplishment. We look forward to your participation in ACL 2021 and to showcasing your work to the broader computational linguistics community.  Kind regards,  ACL 2021 Resource Track Committee   acl2021@softconf.com   Association for Computational Linguistics

full_email_context: Thread ID: RLMZE8 Mail ID: MAILA9X6VJ3M Date: 19th January 2025 From: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> Subject: Confirmation: Section 4.2 Collaborative Drafting Session & Next Steps  Dear Ramesh, Ananya, and Michael,  Thank you all for your prompt feedback and coordinated efforts toward the Section 4.2 revision. I agree with Ramesh that the addition of both the Japanese and Chilean frameworks and the newly-secured NLI case presents a truly comprehensive perspective on regulatory diversity. Ananya, I appreciate your outline and the circulated citation list—I have reviewed these and see several strong alignment points with our primary datasets, particularly regarding annotation workflow documentation and consent scaffolding.  In terms of scheduling, I am available for a collaborative drafting session on 16 January, ideally starting at 14:30 IST, but could accommodate an earlier/later start within the 14:00–17:00 window if that is preferable for all. I suggest we use Google Meet for ease of document sharing and real-time coordination. Here is a provisional link for our session: https://meet.google.com/nmt-ksqj-bve. Please confirm if this platform and timing work, or advise on any alternative preferences.  As a brief agenda: 1. Rapid review of comparative outlines (Ananya’s and Michael’s inputs; my cross-referenced annotations for Indian and UK/EU datasets). 2. Live drafting of the new Section 4.2 content, integrating all jurisdictional insights and reviewer-requested narrative expansions. 3. Detailed mapping of NLI-specific considerations (tiered consent, anonymization, cross-border sharing) and any regulatory divergences noted from Japan/Chile. 4. Delegation of drafting responsibilities for compliance appendices and bibliography harmonization.  If helpful, I can prepare a “track changes” document beforehand to ensure all edits are traceable for subsequent consolidation. Please let me know if you have any specific preparatory materials or outstanding points you wish to address in the session.  Looking forward to a productive drafting phase and to collectively strengthening our manuscript for final submission.  Best regards,  Sunita  Sunita Sen   PhD Scholar   Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

full_email_context: Thread ID: YLV9DF Mail ID: MAILF4Y8S2MW Date: 14th April 2022 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> Subject: Harmonized Embargo Log – Oxford Compliance Note and Final Confirmation  Dear Michael, Sunita, and Prof. Bhatia,  Thank you for the collaborative review and improvements to the embargo monitoring log. I have completed the compliance check from the Oxford side and can confirm that all terminology and outlined procedures now fully align with our legal guidance and press office protocols. The new reference to “temporary access restriction” has been reviewed by our legal consultant, and there are no objections to its deployment so long as the final embargo log retains the existing audit trail for any future inquiry.  Michael, your additions under the query resolution protocol are clear, and Sunita’s marginal notes accurately capture the nuance of Indian press protocols. I have annotated a single cell in Sheet 3—simply flagging the timing for legal reconfirmation should Oxford receive a concurrent pre-acceptance press request. However, this is precautionary and requires no structural revision.  In light of this, I formally endorse approval and joint sign-off of the harmonized embargo log as version-locked for the JOCCH workflow, effective 14th April 2020. Once you and Sunita have archived the PDF master copy, I will distribute it to our press office and recommend that all partners notify their communications teams accordingly.  Thank you all for your strong attention to both procedural detail and international compliance standards in what is a particularly sensitive communications phase for our consortium. Prof. Bhatia, I look forward to the circulation of the draft press query response template next week and will be ready to field any Oxford-specific escalations as needed.  Best regards,  Ananya  Dr. Ananya Chatterjee   Department of Computer Science   University of Oxford

full_email_context: Thread ID: NHAV29 Mail ID: MAILZ59UNGJQ Date: 27th May 2024 From: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Resource Hosting Venues Table, Dataset Note Structure & User Study Survey Draft  Dear Sunita, Ramesh, and Ananya,  Thank you all for your commitment to advance our work and for the resources being gathered ahead of the 24 April planning session. Sunita, your initiative in assembling the annotation logs and metadata is much appreciated and will form a solid foundation for both the extended paper and the resource publication.  As requested, I’ve attached (in the shared drive folder “2024_JournalExtension/Resource-Dissemination”) a preliminary comparison table of potential dataset hosting venues: Zenodo, CLARIN, and LDC. The table summarizes key factors like repository longevity, data licensing norms, mandatory metadata fields, DOI assignment, and options for access restrictions (should we wish to set embargo periods or limit downloads for research tracking). I’ll be happy to discuss the comparative advantages, and if there are additional platforms of interest (e.g., institutional repositories, HuggingFace Datasets), let me know so I can expand the survey.  For the dataset/resource paper, I’ve outlined a draft structure that aligns with both JOCCH dataset notes and LREC resource papers. The main sections I propose are: (1) Corpus construction and annotation pipeline, (2) Annotation guidelines and normalization methods, (3) Inter-annotator agreement metrics and quality control, (4) Release logistics and access protocols, and (5) Documentation of the user study framework. Ananya, your suggestion to include survey instruments and uptake tracking in the appendix is spot on.  I’ve uploaded an initial draft of the user study survey, focusing on corpus usability, representativeness of historical scripts, and NLP pipeline compatibility. Sunita, please review and feel free to comment or add custom questions regarding annotated data formats and linguistic phenomena coverage.  Let’s aim to finalize talking points for the meeting agenda and agree on division of writing/liaison tasks as part of our next call. Looking forward to everyone’s feedback.  Best regards,  Michael  Dr. Michael Bradley   Department of Computer Science   Stanford University

I am pleased to share the meeting minutes to ensure we are aligned on operational and outreach priorities while our JOCCH submission (SUB-JOCCH-2022-0362) proceeds through review.  **Meeting Minutes – 13th March 2020**  **Attendees:** Sunita Sen, Dr. Michael Bradley, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee   **Duration:** 15:30–16:05 IST / 11:00–11:35 BST  **Agenda and Discussion Points:**  1. **Embargo Compliance Review**    - Michael confirmed successful embargo activation for both the Zenodo dataset and GitHub supplement, with reviewer-only secure access via private tokens and visible embargo notification (as previously circulated).    - Prof. Bhatia advised logging embargo confirmation in the IACS data tracker, which Michael completed, and sharing embargo compliance language with the JOCCH editorial office if requested.  2. **Outreach Materials Coordination**    - Sunita and I finalized our division of labor: I will draft the departmental/research-focused summary by 18 September, while Sunita will shape the general audience release; both versions will reside in the new shared folder for iterative feedback.    - Michael will review for accuracy and adapt embargo language as necessary for external audiences.    - We agreed to prepare a brief embargo status statement to append to all initial releases.  3. **Timeline Alignment and Internal Communication**    - A biweekly internal email check-in was scheduled; Ananya will circulate reminders. If reviewer feedback is received, an immediate group discussion will be convened.  **Action Items:** - Ananya: Draft Oxford/Stanford departmental abstract by 18 Sept, coordinate internal reminders. - Sunita: Prepare IACS/social media version by 19 Sept. - Michael: Monitor for any editorial office embargo queries and coordinate content review. - Prof. Bhatia: Oversee data compliance status; review outreach drafts before external release.  Thank you all for your collegiality and seamless organization—please edit or expand these minutes as needed.  Best regards,  Ananya  Dr. Ananya Chatterjee   Department of Computer Science   University of Oxford

full_email_context: Thread ID: ALQNXI Mail ID: MAILE9T7PZD5 Date: 8th August 2019 From: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Re: Coordination Meeting – Final Agenda and Preparation Checklist  Dear all,  Thank you, Michael, for organizing the Zoom meeting and providing a clear agenda. I have received the link and confirm my availability for the meeting today, 30 August, at 15:15 IST. I appreciate everyone’s prompt responses and flexibility in scheduling.  As preparation for our discussion:  - I have drafted the initial template for the point-by-point response letter based on the reviewer reports (SUB-JOCCH-2019-0187). It maps each comment to our planned revisions, with fields for status updates and lead authors per section. I will share this document with edit access on our shared Drive before the meeting. - Ananya, I look forward to your draft for the “Limitations and Future Work” section. If you’re able to circulate the text ahead of the meeting, I can begin integrating it as we work through the response letter. - Prof. Bhatia, your outline for the compliance appendix updates appears comprehensive. Once your draft language and clarifications are ready, we can cross-reference the licensing table with archival statements and ensure full attribution and clarity in the revised appendix. - Michael, please upload the preliminary annotator agreement spreadsheet at your convenience; I’ll review its format for integration into our results section.  During the meeting, I propose we designate primary/secondary reviewers for each document segment, and agree on a timeline for internal feedback to ensure we remain ahead of the 22 September deadline.  Thank you, everyone, once again for your unfailing collaboration and commitment. See you all shortly on Zoom!  Best regards,  Sunita

object_label: joint press release
evidence_sentence: Thank you all for swiftly sharing resources and aligning on the next steps for our joint press release.
full_email_context: Thread ID: VF6U8Q Mail ID: MAILX8C4S9DJ Date: 4th August 2022 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> Subject: Draft Press Release for JCDL 2022 – Initial Circulation & Collaborative Input  Dear Sunita, Ramesh, and Michael,  Thank you all for swiftly sharing resources and aligning on the next steps for our joint press release. Special thanks to Sunita for uploading both the IACS press office template and the excellent sample releases; these will be invaluable as we tailor the announcement to reflect our cross-institutional collaboration.  Attached to this email (“JCDL2022_Press_Release_Draft_v1.docx” in the shared folder), you will find my initial draft. I have followed the IACS guidelines for structure and length, and included the recommended language for funding attributions and author credits. The scientific summary is concise, focusing on our core research contribution—methodologies for multilingual, legally compliant NLP on historical media datasets—and the innovative FAQ protocols we developed for the JCDL submission.  I have inserted placeholders for institutional quotes (see sections marked [IACS Quote – Ramesh], [Stanford Quote – Michael], [Oxford Statement]), which will further personalize the release. Ramesh, your contextual statement on Indian RTI applications will fit well in the impact paragraph. Michael, a brief note on the value of the Stanford repository for global archival research would be highly welcome. Sunita, I have adapted the standard IACS embargo and legal notice for review and approval before submission.  Please review the draft and provide all tracked comments and suggestions in the Google Doc by 2 March. Ramesh, if you see any deviations from IACS protocol, let me know so we can make corrections before the final press office review. Michael, feel free to suggest Stanford boilerplate language or point out any global audience clarifications that may strengthen our message.  Once all feedback is incorporated, I will circulate a revised draft for final approval and then liaise with the respective press offices as discussed. Many thanks again for your coordinated input. I look forward to your suggestions!  Best wishes,  Ananya  Dr. Ananya Chatterjee   Department of Computer Science   University of Oxford

full_email_context: Thread ID: TBVJMZ Mail ID: MAILY7QBRK5C Date: 6th October 2022 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> Subject: Re: Response to Workshop Agenda Feedback & Finalization Steps  Dear Ramesh, Michael, and Sunita,  Thank you, Ramesh, for summarizing and swiftly aligning all final adjustments to the workshop/tutorial agenda. I am delighted to confirm my availability for the proposed time slot of 4:00pm BST / 8:30pm IST / 8:00am PDT, which should serve both the European and North American audiences well.  I appreciate the additions based on everyone’s feedback—particularly the extended breakout session, structured call for lightning talks, and the informal networking slot at the close. I agree that including ethical and hands-on engagement components not only aligns with current best practices in the digital humanities but will also elevate the value of our event for participants of diverse backgrounds.  I will proceed to draft the participant feedback and resource assessment form by 16 May. If you can share any anticipated key learning outcomes or specific feedback metrics you wish to prioritize, kindly send your suggestions in the coming days. The form will incorporate both quantitative (Likert-scale) and qualitative sections to support future reporting and improvement.  For the promotional campaign, please include me in the Google Drive folder for outreach materials so I can adapt the blurb for Oxford’s digital scholarship and computer science networks. I am also happy to cross-post in relevant UK-based mailing lists and digital humanities forums.  Thank you again for your collaboration and attention to detail. I look forward to seeing the supporting materials and participating fully in what promises to be a dynamic and impactful program.  Best wishes,  Ananya  Dr. Ananya Chatterjee   Department of Computer Science   University of Oxford

full_email_context: Thread ID: 1ZO12K Mail ID: MAILM2K4Q5WN Date: 28th August 2022 From: JCDL Communications Liaison <comm@jcdl2022.org> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> CC: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> Subject: Official Launch: JCDL 2022 Newsletter & Next Steps for Conference Promotion  Dear Sunita, Dr. Chatterjee, Dr. Bradley, and Prof. Bhatia,  We are pleased to inform you that the JCDL 2022 program newsletter featuring your project, “NLP Innovations for Historical Texts: Multilingual Heritage Preservation across Continents,” has now been officially published and distributed to our international subscriber base.  You may view the final newsletter here: https://jcdl2022.org/newsletter/March/JCDL2022_MainIssue.html  The newsletter has already begun circulating via direct email, JCDL’s social media channels, and through our partner academic societies. Early analytics indicate strong engagement with your feature, including above-average click-through on the visual schematic and consistent share rates on institutional press releases. We will forward summary readership reports once the distribution cycle concludes.  For continued promotion, we encourage your teams to amplify the newsletter link through your university communication offices and departmental lists. Should you wish to coordinate a thematic social media campaign or provide companion content (e.g., a video introduction or faculty Q&A), please let us know. We would be happy to facilitate further visibility through JCDL’s official platforms in the lead-up to the conference mainstage sessions.  Once again, thank you for your exemplary preparation and collegiality—your group’s contributions are among the highlights of this year’s outreach. Please expect a follow-up message from our events team regarding the scheduling of live project spotlights and possible participation in the conference media day.  Kind regards,  JCDL 2022 Communications Team

evidence_sentence: The automated confirmation reiterated successful receipt of both our main manuscript and all supplementary files.
full_email_context: Thread ID: Q0GAQD Mail ID: MAILWD9CX3N2 Date: 3rd April 2023 From: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> Subject: JCDL 2023 Submission Acknowledgement – SUB-JCDL-2023-1174  Dear Ramesh, Ananya, and Sunita,  I am pleased to report that we have received formal acknowledgment from the JCDL 2023 organizing committee regarding our submission, “Cross-Lingual Semantic Drift Detection and Digital Humanities Applications in Historical Corpora” (Submission ID: SUB-JCDL-2023-1174). The automated confirmation reiterated successful receipt of both our main manuscript and all supplementary files. According to the correspondence, the Program Committee will issue initial decision notifications in February 2023, with reviewer comments following shortly thereafter.  Key points mentioned in the acknowledgement: - All submitted files have passed the technical compliance checks for the JCDL portal.  - Any further updates or correction requests must be made by 6 December, after which the submission will be locked for review. - The organizing committee appreciates the clarity and completeness of our supplementary materials—particularly the annotation pipeline flowchart and compliance metadata. - All correspondence regarding our submission will cite the Submission ID: SUB-JCDL-2023-1174, and Ananya (as our point of contact) will receive primary communications. - Expected timeline: Initial review results around 31st May 2021.  I have attached a PDF copy of the formal acknowledgement for everyone’s records. Ananya, please do let us know if you receive any direct queries from the Program Committee or need support in responding. In the meantime, I agree with our plan to draft the arXiv preprint version once we have final compliance clearance.  Looking forward to the next steps, including dissemination and planning for our proposed follow-up research initiatives. Please let me know if anyone needs additional documentation or wishes to discuss extension proposals in the interim.  Best regards,  Michael  Dr. Michael Bradley   Department of Computer Science   Stanford University

object_label: revising Chilean and Japanese regulatory compliance subsections
evidence_sentence: I have revised the Chilean and Japanese regulatory compliance subsections, adding labeled workflow diagrams for both consent and data transfer phases.
full_email_context: Thread ID: JNOXD5 Mail ID: MAILBPC46YNV Date: 7th March 2025 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> Subject: Compliance Section Updates, Workflow Diagram Feedback, and Next Steps  Dear Sunita, Ramesh, and Michael,  Thank you, Sunita, for circulating such thorough meeting minutes and clearly documenting our action plan following the 8 March coordination call. I wanted to update everyone on my progress with the compliance sections and incorporate the group’s latest feedback before finalizing my contributions.  I have revised the Chilean and Japanese regulatory compliance subsections, adding labeled workflow diagrams for both consent and data transfer phases. Following Ramesh’s suggestion, I ensured that each step includes clear transition markers and compliance checkpoint labels to facilitate cross-referencing with the new manuscript structure. Michael, I’ve also included brief case illustrations based on the institutional guidelines you mentioned in our call, particularly regarding dataset retention and inter-institutional collaboration protocols.  A draft of these updates, along with all diagrams in PNG and SVG formats, is now available in our shared Google Drive folder (“JOCCH Major Revision > Compliance Sections – Ananya Drafts”). Please let me know if you have any trouble accessing the files.  I would appreciate feedback from all of you, but especially Ramesh, regarding whether the integration points and narrative flow align with your restructuring plan for the main text. Michael, your insights on the overlap with annotation metadata—especially as it pertains to labeling and terminology—would be valuable to ensure consistency.  Sunita, do let me know if the diagrams or specific compliance narratives require adaptation for the response letter. I am happy to assist with editing reviewer-point responses corresponding to these sections.  Barring any major changes, I am on track to meet the 13 March deadline for finalized content. Please share any comments or suggestions by the evening of 12 March if possible, so I can implement them promptly.  Thanks again for your collaboration. Looking forward to everyone’s feedback.  Best regards,  Ananya  Dr. Ananya Chatterjee   Department of Computer Science   University of Oxford

Should we provide a supplementary installation guide for Windows/Mac users, or streamline to cloud-based deployment for maximum accessibility?  In addition, Sunita, thank you for setting up the shared drive and GitHub Organization. I have accepted the invites and will upload a draft of the technical setup instructions, as well as a sample notebook, prior to our meeting. I will be prepared with a brief walkthrough of current technical documentation progress and a checklist for group review. If there are any further technical hurdles or content priorities that others would like to raise, I suggest adding them to the shared Google Doc before our call. I have just uploaded my full session notes focusing on accessibility interventions, with a particular emphasis on how we triaged live requests (notably those from participants using screen readers and non-standard browsers). These should provide valuable context for our discussion later.  Based on the data so far, a few immediate takeaways for our documentation and future workshops stand out: - Instant moderator response times (average <2 minutes) for accessibility concerns had a clear positive correlation with satisfaction scores. - Our resource mirror alternatives eliminated nearly all regional download issues, suggesting a model for scalable open dataset dissemination in future events. - Since the annotated NER and OCR pipeline citation queries were so frequent, I propose synthesizing a formal citation protocol—possibly as an appendix in any workshop report or joint submission.  As a preliminary next step, I have started drafting an outline for our workshop report (preliminary structure: Introduction, Workshop Design and Accessibility, Dataset Overview, Q&A/Moderation Framework, Participant Feedback, Lessons Learned, and Recommendations/Protocols). I suggest we allocate some time during our debrief to refine this outline, divide drafting responsibilities, and establish a timeline for a possible JCDL workshop proceedings or JOCCH submission.  Thank you once again for your collaborative spirit and high standards throughout this project. Looking forward to our discussion and to solidifying plans for collaborative writing.  Best regards,  Sunita  Sunita Sen   PhD Scholar   Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

My annotated comments are now uploaded in the file “Section_4.2_JOCCH_Revision_RB_20Jan2025.docx” under the shared “Drafts” folder.  Key observations and final recommendations:  1. JOCCH Editorial Alignment: Your integration work ensures that all case studies (India, UK/EU, Israel, Japan, Chile) now explicitly respond to JOCCH’s updated compliance guidance on cross-jurisdictional annotation. Michael’s regulatory citations and Ananya’s coordinated harmonization of wording have greatly improved clarity for a non-specialist audience. 2. Consent & Anonymization Protocols: The comparative analysis of consent stratification and anonymization approaches is rigorous and appropriately foregrounds both procedural strengths (e.g., NLI's “tiered consent”) and region-specific limitations (e.g., constraints in annotator metadata retention in Japan and Chile). I added a few clarification notes where further specificity may help, but overall coverage is excellent. 3. Data Transmission & Regulatory Divergences: The inclusion of cross-references to our Indian/EU datasets substantially strengthens the discussion on inter-regional data transmission. I would only suggest a brief bridging sentence in the conclusion to highlight potential research implications for pan-Asian and Euro-Israeli NLP collaborations, as this was specifically alluded to in the reviewer’s final point.  Action Reminder & Next Steps: - Ananya: Please review my marginal comments and, if in agreement, incorporate/resolve them during your bibliography harmonization (target draft by 22 January). - Sunita: Confirm your readiness for a quick “clean version” consolidation once all co-auhtor comments are incorporated. - Michael: All footnotes appear JOCCH-compliant; appreciate your offer to clarify additional translation approaches as needed.  Let’s aim to finalize the camera-ready main text and supporting appendices by 24 January, keeping a short buffer for last-minute editorial tweaks. Please reply if there are any outstanding questions or barriers to consolidation.  Many thanks for the collective attention to detail and collegiality throughout this intensive revision phase. Proud to see our paper approaching submission-readiness in such a comprehensive form.  Best regards,  Ramesh  Prof. Ramesh Bhatia   Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

full_email_context: Thread ID: U3H5YV Mail ID: MAILB72PJD4M Date: 25th February 2022 From: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in> To: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> Subject: Ethics Compliance Update and Clearance for Submission  Dear Michael, Ananya, and Sunita,  I am writing to provide an update concerning the necessary institutional clearances as we prepare to submit our manuscript to JOCCH. As of this afternoon, I have received official confirmation from the IACS Legal and Ethics Committee regarding the open hosting of our annotation protocols, supplementary case study vignettes, and the processed historical corpus on our designated GitHub repository. The committee expressed appreciation for the thoroughness of our documentation, harmonization of multi-source data governance policies, and explicit reference to anonymized adjudication case studies.  A few procedural clarifications were flagged and have now been addressed: - The final README in our Supplementary/CaseStudies directory must contain explicit statements regarding consent for historical data use and clear data licensing terms (I have drafted the required text and uploaded it for your review). - All links in the manuscript referencing external corpus materials must include a persistent DOI or repository release tag; please ensure uniformity across main text and supplement. - While the cross-institutional compliance statement in our cover letter is already strong, the committee suggests one additional line affirming that all collaborative annotations complied with IACS and partner university ethics standards.  With these minor additions, we have full clearance to proceed. Michael, you may now finalize the integrated package, and all team members should verify updated README and licensing statements in the latest commit. Our timeline for full draft review and copyedits by 26 August remains feasible, and we are on track for submission by the 28 August internal target.  Thank you all for your conscientious coordination at this crucial finalization stage. Please notify me if further clarification or signatures are required from IACS or if there are lingering cross-institutional compliance questions.  Best regards,  Ramesh Bhatia   Professor, Department of Computer Science   Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

full_email_context: Thread ID: HZAWMB Mail ID: MAIL2ZRL45TY Date: 28th August 2023 From: Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> To: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> Subject: JOCCH Editorial Update: Minor Revision Requested for SUB-JOCCH-2023-0193  Dear Ramesh, Sunita, and Michael,  I am writing to inform you that we have received an initial editorial response for our JOCCH submission (Submission ID: SUB-JOCCH-2023-0193). The editorial team has completed their preliminary review, and I am pleased to report that the manuscript has been provisionally accepted pending a set of minor revisions. The official communication cites the following points for revision:  1. **Clarification of Dataset Licensing:** The editors request two additional sentences in the Data Availability section specifying license terms for both the annotated corpus and code repository. Their goal is to ensure clear compliance with ACM’s open data policies. 2. **Expanded Figure Legends:** Reviewer feedback indicates that several figure legends—particularly for Figures 2 and 4—would benefit from more precise method captions to improve interpretability for readers less familiar with entity adjudication protocols. 3. **Minor Formatting Corrections:** There are small requests to adjust in-text citation formatting for two heritage text references (pages 10 and 13) and to align the author ORCID listing on the title page.  I have attached the editorial office’s official letter—including tracked annotations—to this email, as well as editorial markups on our PDF. The expected deadline for the revision is 9th September 2021, which should provide us ample time to implement these minor changes.  **Next Steps:** - Sunita, can you please update the Data Availability and licensing segments by 2 June? - Michael, would you be able to refine the figure legends in the manuscript draft and return them to the group by 6 June? - Ramesh, your review of the revised manuscript prior to portal re-submission would be invaluable; I will circulate the full draft for your input by 7 June.  Let us aim for internal approval by 8 June, giving us a comfortable margin ahead of the deadline.  Congratulations and thank you all for your commitment to this collaborative effort. Please let me know if there are any questions regarding the editorial comments or if further clarification is needed from the JOCCH office.  Best regards,  Ananya  Dr. Ananya Chatterjee   Department of Computer Science   University of Oxford

object_label: Accepted
evidence_sentence: your oral presentation submission has been **ACCEPTED** for presentation at ACL 2021.
full_email_context: Thread ID: LJRN13 Mail ID: MAILR6QP7HD4 Date: 14th December 2021 From: acl2021@conferences.aclweb.org To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in> CC: Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Decision Notification – ACL 2021 Oral Presentation (Submission ID: SUB-ACL-2022-1098)  Dear Sunita Sen and Co-authors,  On behalf of the ACL 2021 Program Committee, we would like to thank you for your submission entitled 'A Provenance-Aware Annotation Protocol for NLP on Historical Document Corpora' (Submission ID: SUB-ACL-2022-1098).  After careful consideration, we are pleased to inform you that your oral presentation submission has been **ACCEPTED** for presentation at ACL 2021.  The reviewers commended your work for its methodological rigor, the relevance of the provenance-aware approach for historical NLP corpora, and the practical handling of linguistic diversity and annotation provenance. Additionally, the inclusion of a specialized Q&A section addressing model bias was considered a valuable addition that anticipates ongoing discussions in the community.  Please note the following next steps: - **Camera-Ready Submission Deadline:** 1st January 2020 (23:59 AoE) - You will be required to submit a camera-ready version of your slide deck, any updated supplementary material, and presenter biographical information through the ACL submission portal. - Further details and formatting guidelines will follow in a separate communication.  We congratulate you and look forward to your presentation in August. Should you have questions regarding the next steps, please contact the organizing committee at acl2021@conferences.aclweb.org.  Best regards, The Program Committee   ACL 2021

object_label: Section 4.2 collaborative drafting session; high-level alignment of terminology and structural flow; document-level revisions; assign split tasks for compliance appendix revisions and pending bibliography entries
evidence_sentence: Dear Sunita, Ananya, and Ramesh,
full_email_context: Thread ID: 16OTBY Mail ID: MAILV7PSF4X9 Date: 19th January 2025 From: Dr. Michael Bradley <michael@cs.stanford.edu> To: Sunita Sen <scholar.sunita@iacs.res.in>, Prof. Ramesh Bhatia <ramesh.bhatia@iacs.res.in>, Dr. Ananya Chatterjee <ananya.chatterjee@cs.ox.ac.uk> Subject: Confirmation & Preparation for 16 Jan Section 4.2 Drafting Session  Dear Sunita, Ananya, and Ramesh,  Thank you, Sunita, for organizing and circulating the proposed agenda and provisional Google Meet link for today's Section 4.2 collaborative drafting session. I'm confirming my availability for the 14:30 IST start time and the use of Google Meet (the provided link works perfectly on my end).  Ahead of our meeting, I've further annotated the comparative legal matrix with newly integrated rows corresponding to the National Library of Israel's protocols—especially those concerning tiered consent structures and anonymization standards. I’ve also highlighted where NLI’s cross-jurisdictional data flows notably diverge from both Japanese and Chilean approaches. These comments should help us structure the “contrast and synthesis” subsection efficiently during the live drafting.  For the session, I suggest we open with a high-level alignment of terminology and structural flow (to ensure seamless integration into the reviewer-mandated narrative) before diving into document-level revisions. Ananya’s outline provides a strong backbone, and with everyone’s sector-specific annotations, I expect we can produce a first-pass integrated subsection within our slot. Following this, I propose we assign a short list of split tasks for compliance appendix revisions and pending bibliography entries, which can be resolved asynchronously.  Ramesh, your offer to annotate legal divergences within the matrix is well-timed—please upload your notes directly to the shared drive version so we have all perspectives in one place. Sunita, a “track changes” document would be invaluable, especially as we collate regulatory language and cross-reference best practices for management transparency.  Looking forward to seeing everyone at the session and making significant headway toward the February deadline. If anyone encounters access issues or has last-minute materials to discuss, feel free to reply here or ping me via chat.  Best regards,  Michael  Dr. Michael Bradley   Department of Computer Science   Stanford University
